title: Generic algebraicity gives quasi-finiteness over a point of local dimension at most one
statement: Let $g:Z\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $s\in S$. Suppose that $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has Krull dimension at most $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Suppose that for every generic point $\eta$ of every irreducible component of $Z$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the induced extension $\kappa(g(\eta))\subseteq\kappa(\eta)$ of residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is algebraic, meaning that every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(g(\eta))$. Then $g$ is quasi-finite at every $z\in Z$ with $g(z)=s$, in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. No properness, normality, or global Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $z\in Z$ with $g(z)=s$. Choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing $s$ and $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $z$ with $U\subseteq g^{-1}(V)$, and let $\mathfrak p$ represent $s$. Apply [lem-sfb-generic-algebraicity-localized-affine-model] to this chart and the assumed generic algebraicity. It gives the local ring $B=R_{\mathfrak p}$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pB$, the isomorphism $B\cong\mathcal O_{S,s}$, the residue-field identification $k=B/\mathfrak m=\kappa(s)$, and the finite type $B$-algebra $C=A\otimes_RB$. Thus $B$ is Noetherian with $\dim B\le1$. For every minimal prime $Q'$ of $C$, put $q=Q'\cap B$. The same statement gives algebraicity of $\kappa(Q')/\kappa(q)$, with the canonical field maps.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-local-dimension-one-closed-residue-algebraicity] to this $B$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and $C$. Step 1 verifies each hypothesis: $B$ is Noetherian local of dimension at most one, $C$ is of finite type over $B$, and every minimal-prime residue extension is algebraic. Hence every prime $P$ of $C$ contracting to $\mathfrak m$ satisfies $\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(P)=0$, for precisely the field $k=B/\mathfrak m$ fixed in Step 1. This conclusion also covers vertical components and nonreduced rings.

source.place: Tag 0AB6, label lemma-quasi-finite-in-codim-1, proof of condition (2), reduced-component and vertical/horizontal dimension-inequality paragraphs (returned proof steps 5–7).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-localized-affine-residue-criterion-quasifinite] to the original locally finite type morphism $g$, the same chart $U\to V$, and $s$. Its rings $B,C$ and field $k$ are exactly those of Step 1, and Step 2 supplies its condition for every prime over $\mathfrak m$. The cited statement identifies $U_s$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/\mathfrak mC)$, proves that space finite and discrete, and concludes that $g$ is quasi-finite in $Z,S$ at every $u\in U$ over $s$. In particular it is quasi-finite at the chosen $z$. Since $z$ was arbitrary, the assertion follows.
